accordance with the attached ordinance. No direct financial impact to the County will occur as	
a result of this petition.

m-jacksonville|2025-01-07|d27e6bf8|2771d.title:
Mary Staffopoulos of the Office of General Counsel discussed a draft resolution and a draft list of possible “guardrails” for allocation of the funding to the Council’s chosen priorities. The resolution calls on the Mayor to put the 0.5% of the General Fund budget ($9.4M) required by the Ordinance Code into a Council Strategic Initiatives Contingency account for the Council to determine uses throughout the fiscal year. The guardrails could be included now, discussed at the budget hearings later in the year, or both. Council Member Pittman cautioned that many small non-profits don’t have sufficient budgets to provide services with their own funds and then get paid back on a reimbursement basis by the City and asked for consideration of alternatives to assist those agencies. Council Member Freeman said providers that work on an academic year and school-related programs are at a disadvantage because of the fiscal year calendar and its relation to the grant cycle and said Code Chapter 118 may need to be amended to deal with their issues. 

Motion (Arias/2nd Freeman): approve filing of the resolution as drafted and discuss addition of guardrails later in the year – approved by consensus of the committee without objection.

Report #886: Budget Summary Fiscal Year 2024/25: the report summarizes council’s action during the budget process.

Report #781C: Follow-Up on Animal Care and Protective Services Audit: all outstanding items were cleared, and the audit is closed.

Report #811B: Follow-Up on Mobility Fees Audit: all outstanding items were cleared, and the audit is closed.

Report #887: Quarterly Summary for the Twelve Months Ended September 30, 2024: Regarding the independent authorities, JEA has over $100M of surplus and has an ordinance pending today to reduce debt by applying those surplus funds to pay-go capital in place of borrowing.  Three of JTA’s operating divisions exceeded budgetary authority due to increased expenditures in excess of Council approved appropriation authority so a budget reconciliation amendment will be needed as in past year. JaxPort ended the year with a surplus of approximately $11 million. JAA had a budget surplus of $45.1M at year-end due to reduced expenditures caused by Concourse B construction project delays. 

The Special Events Fund exceeded budgetary authority by $33,000 and has a negative cash balance of $180,000. The Building Inspection Fund is about to hit its state law cap on retained earnings. The Solid Waste Fund has a $3.4M positive variance after an accounting situation was corrected.

Trista Carraher, Auditor's Office explained the amendment, which was approved unanimously via a voice vote. 
Council Member Howland said the budget for the SalesForce project continues growing from $1M to over $2.3M due to expansions of the project scope and wants to know where the cost savings from efficiency will come from. The funds are from the Mayor’s transition task force $25M allocation and excess funds there should have been used for other projects.
Wanyonyi Kendrick, Technology Solutions, said IT’s budget is lower than in previous years and they have saved $6.2M in the 15 months they’ve been in office. She asked that the bill be withdrawn and the $200,000 can go towards other uses as they have found savings elsewhere to pay for SalesForce.

m-jacksonville|2025-01-23|0b45e88b|9ca6d.title: Council Auditor Kim Taylor said the original audit identified 14 issues, of which 2 still remain as of this follow-up: understatement of franchise fees submitted to the City due to insufficient standard operating procedures (SOPs) and lack of testing of the payments, and issues with insurance, payment bonds and reporting. In response to a question from Council Member Lahnen, Ms. Taylor said total revenue from this fee are about $15M. The fee is set at 17% of a company’s gross receipts in the Ordinance Code and the revenue varies by the gross receipts of the companies. Mr. Lahnen asked if the administration is still pursuing the citywide fee study that was announced at the beginning of the Deegan administration; Scott Wilson of the Mayor’s Office said he will check. Ms. Taylor said an annual fee study is required by the Ordinance Code and that requirement was waived by the Council in recent years as part of the budget ordinance. It has not been waived in the last 2 years although no report has been submitted.

m-jacksonville|2025-02-04|d4f1cd71|34739.title: Council Member Howland posed several questions to Economic Development Officer Ed Randolph. Mr. Randolph said the final invoice has not yet been received from the airline but should be within several weeks. He explained that the incentive is for marketing expenses for 10 new routes out of JIA, made in the form of a cash grant from the General Fund. Mr. Howland said he understands the FAA has recently given a clarifying ruling that airports can make marketing grants to airlines either in cash or via reduced landing and other fees. He wants to defer the bill and ask the Jacksonville Aviation Authority to prove that they can’t find $892,000 in their budget to pay this incentive since they have so much cash on hand and had $40M in net income last year. m-jacksonville|2025-10-07|26780e22|d8616.title:
Presentation by Groundwork Jacksonville on Emerald Trail

Greer Johnson-Gillis, Jacksonville Transportation Authority, presented updates for the Emerald Trail. She began with accomplishments for FY 25. She stated that JTA created an action plan based on industry feedback and collaborated with stakeholders like the City, Florida Department of Transportation, JEA, CSX, and Norfolk Southern. She stated that PD&E and 30 percent of the design were completed for Segment 3, with an advertisement for RFP pending. She said that they kicked off the PD&E and conceptual design phase for Segments 4, 6, 7, and 8. 

She said that they maintained federal grant eligibility to align with former and future grant requirements. She stated that stakeholder coordination was critical to the project's success and prioritized cultivating public support and enthusiasm. To this end, they held five community meetings this year and plan to hold a community meeting for all segments in November at Florida State College of Jacksonville. They also conducted community walks in all segment locations and ensured they reached out to community members in the neighborhoods. She stated that they engaged over 300 residents and stakeholders across the city. 

Looking ahead to FY 26, Ms. Johnson-Gillis stated they would continue collaborating with stakeholders and engaging with the community. She noted that the design RFP advertisement for Segment 3 will begin this quarter, with the design phase starting in 2026.

Presentation on JALA Eviction Diversion Program:

CM Boylan introduced the presenters of the Eviction Diversion Program presentation. He provided some context, stating that August foreclosure filings in metro Jacksonville rose 29.24 percent compared to a year ago, while the state's rose 16.35 percent, adding that Jacksonville's foreclosures were double the national foreclosure rate. He invited presenters to the podium to make their presentation.

Melanie Patz, President and CEO of United Way Northeast Florida, began the presentation, which was joined by representatives of Jewish Family and Community Services, Jacksonville Area Legal Aid (JALA), and the courts. City Council provided funding for 2024; for 2025 and 2026, funding was provided through the Mayor's transitional funding recommendations, which are federal dollars. 

Explaining the program, Ms. Patz stated that landlords must consent to tenants' participation to ensure good standing. Also, payments go to the landlords to prevent fraud. If fraud is detected, Jewish Family and Community Services provides those details to JALA, which then reviews the situation and reports to the City, JSO, and the State Attorney. She added that there have not been any fraudulent payments to date.
